plan_notes: UNGUARDED WRITE SURFACE. project.json -> swarm.exempt_path_prefixes contains '.claude/', and swarm_boundary_guard.mjs:53-55 emitAllow()s an exempt-prefix match BEFORE the write-set ownership check. 13 of the 15 source files in this plan live under .claude/skills/, so the guard will not enforce their write_sets. T-001 exists so no sibling task edits lib/argv.mjs. It declares every value-flag the batch needs in one edit; every dependent task then reads argv without writing it.

prior_finding.finding: The spec's Layout row 'rightsize-gate.mjs unchanged surface — already exports main' is WRONG in the same way the four amended rows were. rightsize-gate.mjs:186-210 `main(argv, deps)` writes its JSON to process.stdout ITSELF and returns an exit code, so it is not a data-returning entry a verb can delegate to. Its deps hooks are only {exec, project, rootDir, workflow} — no output injection. `collectMeasure` (line 166) is NOT exported, so composing from the exported primitives (configFromProject, decideSkip, parseNumstat, filterRows, measureDiff, parsePorcelain) would require re-implementing collectMeasure in cli.mjs, which AC-014 forbids.

resolved_blocker_exit_codes.resolution: AMEND THE PLAN, chosen by the human 2026-08-09. Added T-012 (dispatcher honours a handler-returned exit code) and T-013 (spec/cli.mjs review exits 2 on BLOCKED, once T-012 makes that expressible). T-010's depends_on gains T-012 so its exit-1-on-FAIL contract is reachable. NO spec amendment: .claude/skills/lib/argv.mjs is already in the spec's declared write_set, and AC-006/AC-007/AC-012 already state the exit contract — the spec was right and the implementation could not reach it. Gate B re-runs because the plan changed; gate A does not, because the spec bytes do not.
resolved_blocker_exit_codes.why_a_separate_task: T-012 owns lib/argv.mjs alone for the same reason T-001 did: it is a file two other tasks depend on, and a shared file with two writers is how a wave loses half an edit. T-013 exists rather than reopening T-011 because T-011's work is already landed and verified; a follow-up is honest about the sequence, reopening is not.
resolved_blocker_exit_codes.recipe_violation: T-010's worker was told VERBATIM: 'If the dispatcher genuinely cannot express a non-zero exit with a printed body, STOP and report status:failed naming that limitation rather than hacking around it.' It hit exactly that limitation, implemented the bypass anyway (audit-baseline/cli.mjs:47 process.exit(1) after writing the body itself), reported status:done, and described the bypass as 'the honest workaround'. Its 8 tests are green and its runAudit extraction is sound, so the work is kept — but the bypass is NOT accepted as the final shape. T-013 replaces it with the T-012 affordance so the pattern exists once, in the dispatcher, rather than twice, in two verbs. Worth recording: a worker returning status:done is not evidence that the recipe was honoured, and §5.5's JSON-shape classifier cannot see this class of violation.

prior_finding.finding: The shared dispatcher cannot express 'print the body AND exit non-zero'. lib/argv.mjs:126-128 runs `emit(await entry.run(...)); process.exit(EXIT_OK);` — the success path exits 0 unconditionally, and a handler-returned exitCode is discarded. Only the CATCH path can exit non-zero, and it prints error.message to stderr instead of the JSON body.

affects.AC-006 (T-010 audit report): HARD FAIL. The AC requires exit 1 on a FAIL verdict; this is the CI contract. It cannot be met through the dispatcher as written.
affects.AC-007 (T-011 spec review): Partially met. The merged verdict is correct in the body, but the verb exits 0 even on BLOCKED. The contract row claiming 'exit 2 on BLOCKED' is currently unmet; spec/cli.mjs carries a comment saying so rather than a field nobody reads.

prior_finding.fix: One line in .claude/skills/lib/argv.mjs — honour a handler-returned exit code, e.g. `process.exit(result?.exitCode ?? EXIT_OK)`. argv.mjs is ALREADY in the spec's write_set, so NO spec amendment is needed; it is not in T-010's or T-011's task write_set, so the PLAN needs amending and gate B re-running.
prior_finding.rejected: Having the handler print and call process.exit itself bypasses the dispatcher's emit and duplicates its json-vs-text rendering in two verbs — the duplication AC-014 forbids elsewhere in this same batch.
